newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch central bank raises special advances rate.
newsitem.headline: Dutch central bank raises special advances rate.

text.p: The Dutch central bank said on Monday it was raising its special advances rate to 2.90 percent from 2.70 percent for a three-day money market pact it will launch at tender on Tuesday.
The bank also raised its secured loans rate -- the equivalent of Germany's discount rate -- from 2.00 percent to 2.50 percent, effective tomorrow.

A Dutch central bank spokesman said the move had been prompted by standard monetary policy to keep the guilder rate in line with that of the mark. The bank had raised the special advances rate to 2.70 percent from 2.50 percent at the end of February.
The bank had raised the special advances rate to 2.70 percent from 2.50 percent at the end of February.
The secured loans rate is broadly similar to Germany's discount rate while the special advances rate is broadly similar to Germany's repo rate.

"This move partly represents a continuation of (the policy) to normalise domestic rates and at the same time looking to currency markets as usual," De Nederlandsche Bank spokesman Jan Paul Korthals Altes said.
"As usual our monetary policy ...is aimed at the maintenance of the guilder's track against the Deutschmark," he added.
Subscriptions to the new special advances pact will be open between 0730 and 0800 GMT on Tuesday and allocations will be announced shortly afterwards.
The new liquidity pact will replace a four-day facility of 2.68 billion guilders expiring on Tuesday.
